response:
The two things that remain true for fractional reserve banking to be effective are that the bank has sufficient reserves to cover the deposits it has received, and that the bank is operating within its regulatory framework. 

The first thing is that the bank has sufficient reserves to cover the deposits it has received, because if the bank doesn't have enough reserves, it can't pay out the deposits when they are withdrawn, which would lead to a bank run and a loss of confidence in the banking system. 

The second thing is that the bank is operating within its regulatory framework, because if the bank is not following the rules and regulations set by the central bank and other regulatory bodies, it can't use fractional reserve banking, and the system would not be able to function effectively. 

Fractional reserve banking depends on these two things because if either of them is not met, the system would not be able to function effectively, and the bank would not be able to use fractional reserve banking.
